evidence.quote: this case report describes for the first time a mixed deep fungal infection of the skin in a dog

patients.label: Case: 8-year-old female intact dog with meningoencephalitis of unknown origin on immunosuppressive therapy and deep fungal skin infection

identity_evidence.quote: An 8-year-old female intact Elo diagnosed with meningoencephalitis of unknown origin (MUO)
An 8-year-old female intact Elo, diagnosed with immune-mediated brain inflammation

summary.text: An 8-year-old female intact dog with meningoencephalitis of unknown origin was treated with prednisolone at a maintenance dose of 0.5 mg/kg once daily and ciclosporin at a maintenance dose of 6.8 mg/kg twice daily. After 48 weeks of therapy she developed ulcerative dermatitis on the tail, and papular to nodular lesions in the nasal cavity appeared four weeks later.

Cytology and fine needle aspiration of the lesions showed fungal hyphae. Histology showed severe pyogranulomatous deep dermatitis with intralesional conidia in nasal tissue and septated hyphae in tail tissue. Culture and ITS PCR identified Purpureocillium sodanum in the tail lesions and Alternaria rosae in the nasal lesions, and EUCAST microdilution MICs were measured. Urine fungal culture found no fungal organisms, urine showed bacterial cystitis with Escherichia coli, and CT of the head, thorax, and abdomen showed no evidence of fungal invasion.

The cystitis was treated orally twice daily with amoxicillin and clavulanic acid. The dog received systemic itraconazole at 5 mg/kg once daily, topical posaconazole for the tail lesions and topical terbinafine for the nasal lesions, and ciclosporin was halved to 6.8 mg/kg once daily to avoid overdosing when combined with itraconazole.

The fungal lesions did not regress, and the neurological condition worsened despite an increase in the prednisolone dose. She was euthanised because of the severe deterioration in her quality of life.
